One URL. Three exchanges.

$ npx flux-proxy

The catch, printed.

Can FLUX break my app?
The default levers are lossless: compacted schemas decode identically, removed duplicates are exact, prefix repair reorders without deleting, and the reducer never throws — a failure returns your request untouched. Lossy levers stay off until a replay gate proves on your own recorded requests that quality held. Full answer
Why a range and not one number?
Savings depend on your traffic’s shape. The quote comes from your own export and names your segment; sometimes the verdict is literally do not pay us. The bands, by segment
How is billing a counterfactual dispute-proof?
The way energy performance contracts have done it since 1995: a defined baseline, provider-verbatim measurements, an agreed adjustment method. Every request writes an append-only hash-chained event; the invoice is a pure function over those events. Methodology
What do you do with my prompts?
Analysis runs locally; prompts never leave your machine. The ledger records usage numbers, lever names and hashes — not content. Your API key passes through the proxy verbatim and is never stored.
Where does FLUX lose?
Busy interactive agents cap around 29% before cache enablement; already-optimised stacks get 0–5% and a do-not-pay-us verdict; a free trimmer may be all you need if you don’t need the saving verified. The honest comparison
Are these numbers real?
Every figure traces to a runnable command and a commit. The bands are simulator-measured at published provider prices and labelled so; the 9.3% receipt above is real traffic. Your pilot replaces all of it with your own number before any fee exists. Evidence
